svg.title: Four Checks Before a Binding Commitment
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-statutory-and-exposure-decision-tree; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before a Binding Commitment; subtitle: Proceed only when authority, funding, outreach, and purchasing-group structure are documented.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: These are sequential yes-or-no operating checks. Contractual licensing requirements and the internal credit policy are distinct from statutory duties. A failed check routes the account to the stated corrective action rather than silently advancing to execution.; caption: Keep the supporting contract, funds evidence, outreach basis, and member mandate with the opportunity record. Statutes do not grant vendor transfer rights, and a customer signature does not eliminate annual vendor commitment exposure.; stages: label: Authorized licensing route?; value: Yes proceed; no obtain valid authority; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Verify the customer mandate and applicable CSP, CPOR, VIP Marketplace, Zoom, or GPO agreement. Reject unauthorized cross-tenant seat pooling; use the vendor-approved transfer process or retain the existing arrangement.; label: Annual exposure fully covered?; value: Yes proceed; no defer the commitment; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Require cleared customer funding covering the committed NCE exposure and monitor ACH return or card dispute risk. Recurring debit authorization is a collection mechanism, not proof of irrevocable annual funding.; label: Outreach route permitted?; value: Yes proceed; no redesign the contact method; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Apply 47 U.S.C. 227 and applicable FCC rules to calls and texts. Under 16 CFR 310.3 and 310.6(b)(7), do not treat business solicitation as exempt from specified deception prohibitions; assess relevant state calling requirements.; label: GPO conduct independently defensible?; value: Yes execute; no obtain structure-specific review; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Assess competitor coordination under 15 U.S.C. 1. Preserve independent member purchasing decisions, restrict competitively sensitive information, document rebate ownership, and exclude downstream price coordination from the member arrangement.
